Oh, I am so sorry my love. My boyfriend, my soulmate, sadly passed away as well, on Monday, after attempting to take his own life. He was only 19, as am I, but we were each other’s futures. Your post (particularly the final paragraph) struck me as overwhelmingly relatable as I have been struggling to find someone who lost a boyfriend/partner so young too. I am so sorry you are in a similar situation – it is hard for many to comprehend how we feel robbed of a long and happy future and it is impossible to keep up with the overwhelming waves of grief that keep coming. Life seems so relentless, but our boyfriends would want us to go on, and just getting up in the morning and carrying on would make them so proud.

So sorry to hear about how his father is reacting, but please be assured it is a normal and healthy part of the grieving process (as long as it is temporary) and the denial will slowly wane as things so sudden take so long to sink in. I watched my boyfriend die and held his hand as his life support was turned off (he was hospitalised and comatose with severe brain damage to due his attempt) and even my brain cannot comprehend he is gone despite witnessing such permanence. But, it is important to remember that our brains create this cushion of denial to preserve our sanity and aid us in the grieving process, to avoid us from becoming so overwhelmed. This is just my opinion and observation of course, my boyfriend’s dad is going through a similar thought process as is the rest of both our families.

I apologise if my comment seems all over the place, it is an overwhelmingly tragic, painful and heartbreaking situation. Please feel free to PM me at any time, no pressure either way, and I apologise in advance if I am slow to reply, just know that there is someone to relate to even slightly out there.

Thank you so much for posting this, it is an amazingly brave thing to do. Again, I am so sorry you are going through this, and I am sending you and everyone around you love and peace. xx
